threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot a newbie by their confusion at the bus routes—especially when the 38 goes missing. It's like a rite of passage around here.
Caught a bloke on the 333 singing Adele at the top of his lungs last night. The driver turned up the music to drown him out. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a guy in a full suit arguing passionately with a street musician over who’s got the better taste in jazz.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Kebab stand that also doubles as an art gallery, featuring local artists on the walls while you wait for your dürüm.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Real locals know the exact moment the fog rolls in—it's like a blanket, but tourists just think it's a cloudy day.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a dude try to use an umbrella as a walking stick while waiting for the delayed Muni. Only in SF do you see that kind of creativity on a rainy day.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the façades; they miss the real vibe in the alleys after sunset, where locals actually hang out.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their reluctance to break out the Catalan when ordering – it’s all ‘gràcies’ and ‘hola’ but the menus are still a puzzle.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the 48 bus pulls up late, like it's some betrayal. All the locals just roll their eyes and check their phones.
Saw a guy on the 35 last night bickering with a pigeon like it was his long-lost mate. Only in Brixton, right? The pigeon seemed unbothered.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the corner Kebab shop started knowing my order by heart, and the old lady at the bakery always had my favorite Brötchen set aside.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice the U-Bahn stops at a complete standstill during a Streik? Everyone just pulls out snacks and starts chilling, like it's a picnic.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know that the BART delays are just an invitation to grab a taco at Taqueria La Cumbre instead of stressing over the schedule.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 down on Market when it stopped mid-ride for a random karaoke session. Guy in a hoodie belted out ‘Livin' on a Prayer.’ Classic SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just for Gaudí and cafés, but they miss the Sunday afternoon potlucks at local plazas that truly bring the community together.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a new arrival by their hesitance to order the local tapas like patatas bravas—most get lost trying to pronounce it.
